slides.title: Algorithm Efficiency

blocks.text: An algorithm is a sequence of instructions executed by a computer system to solve a given problem.
The efficiency of an algorithm is expressed in terms of its time and space efficiency.
The time efficiency is the execution time of the algorithm.
The space efficiency is the memory space used.
The analysis of algorithms involves categorizing an algorithm in terms of its time and space efficiency.

slides.title: Simple Example: Washing Dishes

blocks.text: Suppose washing a dish takes 30 seconds and drying a dish takes an additional 30 seconds.
Therefore, n dishes require n×60 seconds to wash and dry.
Now suppose we were careless and splashed water around.
This requires us to re-dry all previously washed dishes after washing each additional dish, which is very inefficient.
After washing dish 2, we should dry dishes 1 and 2.
After washing dish 3, we should dry dishes 1, 2, and 3.

slides.title: Problem Size

blocks.text: For every algorithm we want to analyze, we need to define the size of the problem
For the dishes problem, the size of the problem is the number n of dishes that we want to wash and dry.
For a search algorithm, the size of the problem is the number n of elements in the search pool.
For a sorting algorithm, the size of the problem is the number n of elements to be sorted.

slides.title: Growth Function

blocks.text: We must decide what we are trying to efficiently optimize
Time complexity is the execution time
Space complexity is the memory space allocated by the algorithm
Execution time is generally the focus
A growth function is the execution time of an algorithm as a function of the problem size n.
Growth function of the inefficient dishwashing algorithm is 𝑡(𝑛) = 15𝑛2 + 45𝑛

slides.title: Asymptotic Complexity

blocks.text: Asymptotic complexity is based on the dominant term of the growth function. The term that increases most quickly as n increases.
The dominant term for t(n) = 15n2 + 45n is 15n2
Typically, it is not necessary to know the exact growth function for an algorithm.
We are mainly interested in the asymptotic complexity of an algorithm, the general nature of the algorithm as n increases.

slides.title: Big-O Notation

blocks.text: The coefficients and the lower order terms become increasingly less important as n increases
We say that the algorithm is of order n2, written 𝑂(𝑛2)
This is called Big-O notation
There are different Big-O categories: 𝑂(𝑛), 𝑂(𝑛2), etc.

Two algorithms that have the same order of execution time are considered to have the same efficiency and belong to the same category, but this doesn't mean they have equal growth functions or behave exactly the same for all values of n.

slides.title: Example

blocks.text: An algorithm has a quadratic time complexity = O(n2)
Suppose that we use a new processor which is 25 times faster than the old processor
If the maximum problem size for the algorithm is N on the old processor, what is the maximum problem size that we can run on the new processor in the same amount of time?
Solution: The maximum problem size on the new processor with 25X speedup is 25𝑁2 = 5𝑁. This is because the time complexity = O(n2) and 5𝑁2 = 25 × old execution time 𝑁2

slides.title: Why is Analysis of Algorithms Important?

blocks.text: Analysis of algorithms is a fundamental aspect of computing that involves evaluating the performance of algorithms.
This is needed to predict the behavior of an algorithm for large inputs, resulting in scalable software.
It is very convenient to have simple measures for the efficiency of an algorithm than to implement the algorithm and test its efficiency on a computer system.
By analyzing different algorithms, we can compare them to determine the best one for our purpose.

blocks.text: First determine the order of the loop body, then multiply it by the number of times the loop will execute

The number of loop iterations is equal to n
Therefore, the time complexity of the loop is 𝑂(𝑛)

blocks.text: There is a loop inside printsum that repeats count times.
The method is called n times with count = 1, 2, …, n.
The for loop inside printsum is executed 1 + 2 + ⋯+ 𝑛= 𝑛×(𝑛+1) iterations and has a time complexity = 𝑂(𝑛2)

slides.title: Exercise

blocks.text: Determine the growth function 𝑡(𝑛) and order of execution time in Big-O notation of the following nested loops:
for (int i=0; i<n; i++)
for (int j=0; j<n; j += 2)
System.out.println(i + ", " + j);
Solution: The outer for loop is repeated 𝑛times. The inner for loop is repeated 𝑛/2 times.
The growth function 𝑡(𝑛) = 𝑛× 𝑛/2 = 𝑛2/2
The order of execution time is 𝑂(𝑛2)

slides.title: Exercise

blocks.text: Determine the growth function 𝑡(𝑛) and order of execution time in Big-O notation of the following nested loops:
for (int i=0; i<n; i++)
for (int j=1; j<n; j *= 2)
System.out.println(i + ", " + j);
Solution: The outer for loop is repeated 𝑛times. The inner for loop is repeated log2 𝑛times.
The growth function 𝑡𝑛= 𝑛× log2 𝑛
The order of execution time is 𝑂(𝑛log2 𝑛)
